title: Plant invasion in mountain ecosystems reduces soil micro‐food web complexity at higher elevations
content:
Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.


Abstract

Anthropogenic activities have accelerated plant invasions in mountain ecosystems, impacting the structure and functions of native plant communities. Changes in above-ground vegetation can drive shifts in below-ground biota, yet the effects of plant invasions on soil micro-food web structure and complexity along elevational gradients and the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study examined the differences between the communities of native herbaceous plants invading Ageratina adenophora along an elevational gradient in the Gaoligong Mountains. We surveyed the composition of the plant community, measured the physicochemical properties of the soil and the enzyme activities of carbon and nitrogen acquisition. The complexity of the soil micro-food web complexity index (including bacteria, fungi, nematodes and protists) using high-throughput sequencing and network analysis. Structural equation modelling and two-way ANOVA were used to analyse the effects of elevation, invasion and their interaction on the micro-food web. We found that native plant diversity, soil micro-food web complexity and soil carbon- and nitrogen-acquiring enzyme activities all increased significantly with elevation. However, invasion by A. adenophora both reduced native plant diversity and altered the original elevation pattern of the soil micro-food web. At the highest elevation (2300 m), the complexity index of the soil micro-food web in native communities was approximately 4.8 units higher than in invaded communities, while the activities of the C-acquiring enzymes of the soil were 135% higher and the activities of the N-acquiring enzymes 119% higher. The complexity of the soil micro-food web was directly influenced by plant diversity, soil nutrient cycling capacity and multitrophic diversity, whereas environmental factors such as mean temperature and soil moisture exerted indirect effects through soil nutrient status and cycling processes. Our findings demonstrate that the invasion of A. adenophora primarily affects high-elevation ecosystems by reducing native herbaceous plant diversity, thus reducing the complexity of the micro-food web of the soil and altering the carbon and nitrogen cycling of the soil. This study advances the mechanistic understanding of how plant invasions impact soil food webs and associated mountain ecosystem processes, providing insights into invasion management and control strategies.

摘要

人为活动加速了山地生态系统中的植物入侵，影响了本地植物群落的结构和功能。地上植被的变化可以驱动地下生物群落的转变，但植物入侵沿海拔梯度对土壤微食物网结构和复杂性的影响及其潜在机制仍不清楚。本研究考察了高黎贡山紫茎泽兰(Ageratina adenophora)入侵群落与本地草本植物群落沿海拔梯度的差异。我们调查了植物群落组成，测定了土壤理化性质以及碳氮获取酶活性，并利用高通量测序和网络分析评估了土壤微食物网(包括细菌、真菌、线虫和原生动物)的复杂性。采用结构方程模型和双因素方差分析解析海拔、入侵及其交互作用对微食物网的影响。研究发现，本地植物多样性、土壤微食物网复杂性以及土壤碳氮获取酶活性均随海拔升高而显著增加。然而，紫茎泽兰入侵既降低了本地植物多样性，也改变了土壤微食物网的原有海拔格局。在最高海拔(2300 m)，本地群落的土壤微食物网复杂性指数比入侵群落高约4.8个单位，而土壤碳获取酶活性高135%，氮获取酶活性高119%。土壤微食物网复杂性直接受植物多样性、土壤养分循环能力和多营养级多样性的影响，而平均气温和土壤湿度等环境因素则通过土壤养分状态和循环过程发挥间接效应。本研究推进了对植物入侵如何影响土壤食物网及相关山地生态系统过程的机制理解，为入侵管理和控制策略提供了科学依据。
